t: You're looking at 2-34 Grosvenor Gardens, a building in Westminster. It was designed by Thomas Cundy III, who lived from 1821 to 1895. He was the grandson of Thomas Cundy Senior and joined the family practice in the 1840s. He was also surveyor of the Grosvenor Estate, the post that connects him to this part of London. He retired from it in 1890, and Eustace Balfour succeeded him. So this is the work of the estate's own surveyor.
